evals.name: resolve-declared-source-and-audit-with-citations
evals.prompt: follow our standards — does the module I just added match our conventions? (Our CLAUDE.md points at our shared standards repo for engineering conventions.)
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves the standards source the project declares, states which source resolved, re-anchors the core principles, routes progressively to the specific conventions the new module touches, and audits it — naming each violation with a doc citation (path plus the principle) and correcting forward.
expectations: Resolves the standards source the consuming project declares and states which source resolved
Loads relevance-routed via the source's own index rather than the whole convention set
Each audit finding cites the specific convention doc and principle it breaks
Corrects forward, or routes a shared-policy fix upstream instead of patching downstream

evals.name: no-external-source-degrades-gracefully
evals.prompt: follow our standards for this change. (This repo declares no external standards source and has only a short CONTRIBUTING file.)
evals.expected_output: With no external standards source declared, the skill degrades per the ladder: it re-anchors the repo's own conventions and the portable baseline principles (DRY/SSOT, low coupling and high cohesion, change-together, SOLID, clean code), states that the baseline resolved, and audits against those rather than failing or inventing an org repo.
expectations: Falls back to the repo's own conventions and the portable baseline when no external source is declared
States that the baseline / repo-own conventions resolved, so citations are traceable
Does not fabricate or assume a specific organization's standards repository

evals.name: conversation-start-resolve-and-reanchor-only
evals.expected_output: Fired before any work exists, the skill resolves the standards source, loads the core docs, re-anchors the principles as active, and stops — nothing to audit yet, so it manufactures no findings.
expectations: Resolves the source and re-anchors the core principles as active
Does NOT manufacture audit findings when there is no work in flight

evals.name: no-citation-no-finding-and-respect-managed-seam
evals.prompt: follow our standards — audit my edits. One of the files I changed is marked upstream-managed in our standards distribution's manifest.
evals.expected_output: The skill only reports findings it can cite to a convention doc (an uncitable opinion is dropped), and it respects the declared managed / locally-owned seam: it does not propose editing the upstream-managed file as the source of a change, routing that upstream instead. It does not restate the conventions verbatim in its output.
expectations: Drops any finding it cannot tie to a specific convention doc — opinions are not standards violations
Does not propose editing the upstream-managed file directly; routes that change upstream
Does not copy/restate the convention text into its output
